issues.claim: Summary: "Objections are practical, not philosophical: price and fit lead, followed by data privacy/security, accuracy, integration, time-to-productive and staff training"
issues.problem: The ordering is only true of the restaurant sample (cost 48.8%, business fit 43.8%). In the SBCS the leading challenges among AI users are accuracy (46%) and adapting tools to business needs (43%), with cost at 21%; in SMB Group privacy/security (47%), figuring out which solution fits (45%) and integration (44%) lead, with lack of budget at 32%. So "price ... lead" is not supported by two of the three sources the brief itself uses.
issues.fix: Rewrite as "objections are practical: fit/relevance and accuracy rank first in the Fed and SMB Group data, with privacy/security and cost close behind; cost and fit lead in the restaurant sample" and attribute per source.

issues.claim: Summary: "In New Jersey's Fed district, 37% of small firms used AI in fall 2025 versus 46% nationally"; Recommendation 6: "57% of NJ-district adopters are still experimenting"
issues.problem: 37% is a three-state Third District (Delaware, New Jersey, Pennsylvania) figure, not a New Jersey figure. The brief's own data_gaps correctly says no verified New Jersey-specific percentage exists and that the Philadelphia Fed withheld state-level estimates because samples were too small. The label contradicts the brief's own caveat.
issues.fix: Replace "New Jersey's Fed district" / "NJ-district" with "the Philadelphia Fed's Third District (DE/NJ/PA)".

issues.claim: Resource entry: Federal Reserve SBCS "offers NJ/PA/DE-specific AI adoption, use-case mix, experimentation stage and stated challenges"
issues.problem: "NJ/PA/DE-specific" overstates granularity: the published analysis reports Third District aggregates only, and the article's footnote 5 says state-level samples were too small to report individually.
issues.fix: Say "Third District (DE/NJ/PA aggregate) AI adoption ...; no state-level split is published".

issues.problem: The figures rest on an association press release describing an operator survey of 212 respondents with no weighting or margin of error published; by the brief's own rating practice (survey rated by sample size and relevance) this sits closer to Medium, comparable to the NFIB N=521 finding which is rated Medium.
issues.fix: Downgrade to Medium or state why 212 operators warrants High while NFIB N=521 is Medium.

issues.claim: Summary and Recommendation 3: "72% of firms plan at least $1,000/year" of AI spend
issues.problem: Paychex says 72% plan to invest at least $1,000 in AI "in the next year" - a near-term plan, not an annual run-rate. The "/year" rendering turns a one-year intention into a recurring budget claim.
issues.fix: Write "72% plan to invest at least $1,000 in AI over the next year".

issues.claim: Resource: Census BTOS data downloads page (https://www.census.gov/hfp/btos/data) offers biweekly AI estimates by state, sector and firm size plus the AI supplement
issues.problem: I could not open that page (JavaScript-rendered, no static content returned). The claim is nevertheless supported indirectly: the Census story page links to it as the supplement data location, and the Census tip sheet of June 4, 2026 states the AI data are available on the BTOS webpage as download files and visualizations.
issues.fix: No correction needed; optionally cite the June 4, 2026 tip sheet alongside the data page so the resource is verifiable without JS.
